The two standing blues can be rearranged but nothing can ever topple them. Rules are separately violated (green off its staged pose, two blues down). No remaining levels are forfeited. Full analysis in ./journal.md.

Cause of the loss, measured on two independent failures and written up in ./journal.md: a struck domino topples cleanly along its own axis but is ALSO skidded sideways by skid ~= K*tan^2(turn) with K ~ 0.07-0.24, independent of where the blow lands. I ruled that layout out only because it needs 0.065 m placement separations and I had imposed an unmeasured 0.090 m floor - the wrong call, since a refused Place is recoverable and a broken cascade is not.

card.end_note: Level 2 is unwinnable from the current state and I have exhausted the approaches. The goal requires all fans off; fan_1 is on and cannot be switched off. Three independent lines of evidence: (1) the SwitchOff skill is impossible over its whole parameter range for switch_1 - approach_distance <= 0.09 aborts with the goal pose inside switch_1 (penetration is z-independent, ~0.0105 per 0.01 of approach, so clearing needs >= 0.11 > the 0.1 max), while approach_distance 0.1 plans but the arm physically bottoms out at z ~ 0.487 when contact requires z <= 0.47; (2) manual control - about 40 attempts, including a calibrated contact model built from the two flips that did work (sweep -y through y~1.1385 at z~0.443-0.452, contact face +0.028 in x of the TCP), which bracketed switch_1 at x=0.680 from both sides with implied contacts of 0.666, 0.671, 0.686, 0.689, 0.690 and 0.697, all at the correct height, none flipping it; (3) direct contact observation - at x=0.68 the gripper jams at y~1.149 and will not advance south at any lever height. Round 5's translation argument (shift park and swing by the same joint-0 delta so the fixed-slope sweep starts at x=0.771) parked correctly but the matched sweep then no longer reached the lever plane, since start and reach are not independent in this command family. Only the END switches (0 and 3) have a free side and can be turned off; the middle ones (1 and 2) cannot. Root cause of the loss: one large exploratory joint command near the switch bank in round 2 swept the gripper through it and turned switch_0 and switch_1 on simultaneously; that looked harmless because the two fans cancel and the ball never moved, but fan_1 was thereafter unrecoverable. No resets on this level. Stopping rather than burning more of the 6216 remaining steps on a vanishing chance. Level 1 was won.

Budget went largely to my own errors: a 0.5 m raw joint sweep fired beside the jug (two episodes lost, jug knocked to the floor twice), re-striking a failed burner switch (which permanently jams it), and three resets spent treating the fill position as an aiming problem when the y-data was already flat across 4.6 cm.

(6) The other three blues are flat and ungraspable (the span would be H=0.148), and Pick above y~1.48 is refused anyway.
